intro: Back in the attic, Rodolfo and Marcello remember Mimì and Musetta while pretending to work. Caruso and Scotti’s 1907 duet sets tenor against baritone: two men occupy the room, while two absent women occupy their thoughts.
question: How can two singers share a duet while addressing people who are absent?

sections.label: Opening · two remembered loves
sections.mNote: opening listening window, not a timed character entrance

sections.label: Later span · accumulating pressure
sections.mNote: renewed measured build after the quieter middle

cues.title: Tenor beside baritone
cues.text: Throughout the duet, distinguish Rodolfo’s tenor line from Marcello’s baritone. The two men share the attic but remember different women; listen for the difference between an individual phrase and the combined weight of both voices.
cues.evidence: Library of Congress identifies Caruso, tenor, and Scotti, baritone, with orchestra: https://www.loc.gov/item/jukebox-124594/?fo=json . The Royal Opera’s Act IV synopsis supplies their shared recollection. No overlap is timed at zero.

cues.title: Work cannot exclude memory
cues.text: At the start of Act IV, Rodolfo and Marcello try to disguise how much they miss Mimì and Musetta. The same attic that housed Act I’s first meeting now contains two separated lovers, before their friends return with a meagre meal.
cues.evidence: Royal Opera House 2017 programme, Acts I and IV synopses: http://static.roh.org.uk/showings/la-boheme-live-2017/en.pdf . Context for the whole duet, not a word-level timing.

cues.title: A crest leaves breathing room
cues.text: The first broad rise recedes into a lower-level stretch. Keep listening to the accompaniment between the vocal phrases: the duet’s continuity does not require both singers to sustain the same intensity at every instant.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/puccini-o-mimi-tu-piu-non-torni.txt: relative level reaches −13.3 dB at 0:55 and falls to −27.1 at 1:10. The analysis measures combined sound; it does not determine which singer is active.

cues.title: From Murger to the theatre
cues.text: Puccini, Illica and Giacosa turned Henry Murger’s stories into four operatic tableaux. La bohème opened at Turin’s Teatro Regio on 1 February 1896; the two selected duets show the lovers’ meeting and the later cost of separation.
cues.evidence: Puccini Festival biography and work list give authors, source, four-part design and premiere: https://www.puccinifestival.it/en/giacomo-puccini/ . Dramatic comparison follows the Royal Opera’s Act I/IV synopsis.

cues.title: The later build accumulates
cues.text: Across the later stretch, a series of rises sustains the pressure rather than producing one isolated accent. Compare this larger span with the earlier withdrawal, and keep the tenor and baritone distinct even when their sound combines.
cues.evidence: The report shows comparatively high relative-level windows at 2:00–2:20, a retreat around 2:25–2:30 and the highest five-second window at 2:35. No voice separation, key change or exact vocal overlap is inferred.

cues.title: The duet releases its pressure
cues.text: After the later crest, the recorded level withdraws sharply. Let the short ending register against the sustained build before it; in the opera, the men’s recollection is only an early episode in the final act, not its tragic conclusion.
cues.evidence: Relative level falls from −5.8 dB at 2:35 to −27.0 at 2:45 and −52.1 at 3:00. The Royal Opera’s Act IV synopsis places the friends’ meal and Mimì’s return after this opening recollection: http://static.roh.org.uk/showings/la-boheme-live-2017/en.pdf .

transitions.title: The quieter span yields to renewed pressure
transitions.how: The lower-level middle stretch gives way to a sustained renewal. Follow the tenor and baritone as separate lines within the shared accompaniment: their combined sound can enlarge the scene without introducing a third character. This join marks the recorded build after the retreat, not a precisely identified word, cadence or change of orchestral family.
transitions.evidence: Novelty boundaries cluster at 1:42, 1:46 and 1:52. Relative level is around −27 to −25 dB at 1:40–1:50 and rises to −13.5 at 2:00. LOC documents the two vocal roles, but the report cannot isolate them.

transitions.title: The later crest contracts into the ending
transitions.how: The strongest late crest is followed by a marked contraction, leaving a short closing span after the longer build. Compare the length of the withdrawal with the preceding accumulation of attacks. The session’s accompaniment is documented only as orchestra, so the reduction in recorded pressure is not assigned to particular instrumental desks or to an unverified change in scoring.
transitions.evidence: The 2:44 novelty boundary follows the highest five-second window, 2:35. Relative level falls to −27.0 dB at 2:45 and stays low before the final decay. No bar or final vocal release is aligned.

facts: Lucca; Milan Conservatory, 1880–83, with Antonio Bazzini and Amilcare Ponchielli
Publisher Giulio Ricordi · librettists Luigi Illica and Giuseppe Giacosa · later Giuseppe Adami and Renato Simoni
Twelve operas when the three parts of Il trittico are counted separately; songs, sacred and chamber music
composer.background:
Puccini was born into a dynasty of church musicians in Lucca in 1858. His father Michele died when Giacomo was five, and the expectation that the boy would inherit the family profession survived him. Puccini studied locally, played the organ and composed sacred music, including a Mass completed in 1880. Hearing Verdi’s Aida in Pisa in 1876 helped turn his attention towards the theatre. A scholarship enabled him to enter the Milan Conservatory in 1880, where he studied with Antonio Bazzini and Amilcare Ponchielli. His graduation work, the orchestral Capriccio sinfonico, already contains material he would reuse at the beginning of La bohème.

His first opera, Le Villi, failed to win the Sonzogno competition for which it was written, but a performance in Milan in 1884 attracted the publisher Giulio Ricordi. Ricordi supported revisions, further performances and the much less successful Edgar, premiered at La Scala in 1889. The partnership mattered because Puccini composed slowly, demanded repeated alterations to his texts and needed protection against a premature commercial verdict. The theatre was a collective workshop: librettist, publisher, designer and conductor all contributed practical decisions, although Puccini insisted on controlling the length and placement of the decisive moments.
composer.epithet: An opera composer who made a remembered tune, a stage noise or a change of orchestral register determine the timing of a scene.
